Students must not use online or automatic solvers (or similar tools) in an online or take-home Examination unless specifically permitted by the rubric or other module instructions.

process.quote: Where, following an investigation, a decision is made that Serious Plagiarism or a Serious Examination Irregularity has occurred, the case shall become a case of Academic Misconduct under the University Regulations Section 8 - Student Conduct and will be referred to a College Misconduct and Fitness to Practise Committee
An AIO who suspects that plagiarism may have occurred will undertake an investigation, which would normally involve considering evidence.
the student will be given the opportunity to respond to the allegation and will be invited to a meeting (the Academic Integrity Meeting).
The AIO will write to the student notifying them of the concerns and inviting them to the Academic Integrity Meeting.
the meeting may proceed in the student’s absence.
The student can be accompanied to the Academic Integrity Meeting by a Friend, as defined in University Regulation 1.

Where a Student does not agree with the outcome of an Academic Integrity or Examination Irregularity Meeting, the Student may request that their case be considered by a College Misconduct and Fitness to Practise Committee
This outcome should be communicated to the student in writing (the outcome letter), normally within five working days of the Academic Integrity Meeting.
However, a record of the case will be kept on file in order to determine how any future concerns should be handled.

definitions.quote: One form of academic misconduct is plagiarism, which can occur in all types of Assessment when a student claims as their own, intentionally or by omission, work which was not done by that student.

Moderate plagiarism arises when a student fails to follow guidelines on what is regarded as the student’s own original work, including by ignoring conventions or failing to follow acceptable academic practice.
Serious plagiarism arises where there has been reasonably extensive unattributed or incorrectly attributed copying and/or self-plagiarism.
Collaboration between two or more Students in preparing a piece of work that is then presented as their own individual work.
The reproduction in full, or in part, of work the Student has previously submitted
Poor Academic Practice arises where a student has not followed expected academic conventions and may not yet be familiar with the requirements of University level Assessments.

A Minor Examination Irregularity occurs when a student has breached the rules of the assessment, but it can reasonably be determined that this was accidental and was unlikely to have allowed them to gain an unfair advantage in the Assessment.
